evidence.title: Bonaparte Before the Sphinx
evidence.snippet: Bonaparte Before the Sphinx (French: Bonaparte devant le Sphinx) is an 1886 painting by the French artist Jean-Léon Gérôme. It depicts Napoleon Bonaparte during his Egyptian campaign, positioned on horseback in front of the Great Sphinx of Giza, with his army in the background. It popularized Napoleon in front of the Sphinx as a subject in art and caricature. … (Œdipe). evidence.snippet: Victor-Marie Hugo, vicomte Hugo (French: [viktɔʁ maʁi yɡo] ; 26 February 1802 – 22 May 1885) was a French Romantic author, poet, essayist, playwright, journalist, human rights activist and politician. His most famous works are the novels The Hunchback of Notre-Dame (1831) and Les Misérables (1862). evidence.title: Bourbon Restoration in France
evidence.snippet: The Bourbon Restoration was the period of French history during which the House of Bourbon returned to power after the fall of Napoleon Bonaparte in 1814 and 1815. Exiled supporters of the monarchy returned to France, which had been profoundly changed by the French Revolution. Exhausted by the Napoleonic Wars, the kingdom experienced a period of internal and external peace, stable economic prosperity and the preliminaries of industrialisation.

evidence.title: Napoleon
evidence.snippet: Napoleon Bonaparte (born Napoleone di Buonaparte; 15 August 1769 – 5 May 1821) was Emperor of the French from 18 May 1804 until his first abdication in 1814, with a brief restoration during the Hundred Days in 1815. Born on the island of Corsica to a family of Italian origin, Napoleon moved to mainland France in 1779 and was commissioned as an officer in the French Royal Army in 1785. In November 1799 Napoleon engineered the Coup of 18 Brumaire against the French Directory and became First Consul of the Republic.

evidence.title: House of Bonaparte
evidence.snippet: The House of Bonaparte (originally Buonaparte) is a former European imperial and royal dynasty of Italian origin, that was recognized as noble in France under the Ancien Régime. Although the family traces its lineage to the 13th century, the imperial dynasty was established in 1804 by Napoleon I, who was the son of the French Corsican nobleman Carlo Buonaparte and noblewoman Letizia Ramolino. evidence.title: Joseph Bonaparte
evidence.snippet: Joseph Bonaparte (born Giuseppe di Buonaparte, Italian: [dʒuˈzɛppe di ˌbwɔnaˈparte]; Corsican: Ghjuseppe Bonaparte; Spanish: José Bonaparte; 7 January 1768 – 28 July 1844), regnal name José I, was a French statesman, lawyer, diplomat and older brother of Napoleon Bonaparte. In 1806, Napoleon made him King of Naples, and then King of Spain and the Indies in 1808.
